issues.t: V6 burns oil between changes
issues.sym: The oil level drops fast, often a quart every 500 to 1,000 miles, usually starting somewhere past 50,000 miles. You may see blue-gray smoke from the exhaust, or the oil light may flicker on turns or stops.
issues.why: Many owners of the 3.5L V6 report heavy oil use that gets worse with mileage. Owners and shops blame the piston oil-control rings, which can stick or clog and let oil burn in the cylinders. Isuzu often called the rate acceptable.
issues.next: Check the dipstick at every fill-up and keep the level full; the oil light on this engine often comes on too late. If it uses more than a quart per 1,000 miles, have a compression and leak-down test done so you know where the engine stands.

issues.t: Engine knocks or seizes after running low on oil
issues.sym: A sudden knocking or rapping from the engine, loss of power, smoke from under the hood, or the engine locking up, often on a long highway trip. The oil light may not come on first.
issues.why: When the 3.5L V6 burns oil without the owner noticing, it can run so low that the bearings and pistons are starved. Several owners report thrown rods, seized engines and even fires, with replacement engines costing $4,000 to $6,500.
issues.next: If you hear a knock, pull over and shut the engine off. Check the oil before restarting; driving on with a knock can destroy the engine. Have it towed to a shop if the oil was very low or the knock remains after topping off.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping between gears, delayed or harsh shifts, the truck jerking, or no drive at all. Problems often show up after 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in the Trooper (a GM-built unit) wears internally with age and heat. Automatic transmission complaints show up for most model years, and some owners needed a rebuild.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and smell (burnt fluid is a bad sign). Get a scan for transmission codes. If it slips or won't move, stop driving it hard and have a transmission shop diagnose it before it fails completely.

issues.t: Transmission light on with code P1870
issues.sym: The transmission warning light on the dash stays on, and the check engine light may come on too. You might feel a shudder or the engine revving slightly higher at highway speed.
issues.why: Isuzu issued service bulletins for the light coming on with code P1870, which points to the torque converter clutch slipping inside the automatic transmission. Worn internal parts or a valve problem can cause it.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. A fluid service or valve body repair may fix it early; ignoring a slipping torque converter can lead to a full transmission rebuild.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling from leaking intake gaskets
issues.sym: A rough or hunting idle, stalling at low speed, the check engine light with lean codes such as P0171 or P0174, or fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: The intake manifold gaskets on the 3.5L V6 can leak, letting in unmetered air or fuel. Isuzu issued a bulletin about rough idle and lean codes, and owners report gaskets being replaced to fix stalling.
issues.next: Have a shop smoke-test the intake for leaks before replacing sensors. Stalling at low speed is a safety risk, so get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Engine surges or idle stays high
issues.sym: The engine races or the idle stays high, the truck creeps or lunges forward while you are braking, or the gas pedal feels stuck.
issues.why: Owners of these years report surging and high idle. Possible causes include a sticking throttle, a faulty idle control or throttle sensor, or vacuum leaks. NHTSA has no recall for this.
issues.next: If the engine races, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over safely. Have the throttle body, idle control and sensors inspected before driving it in traffic again.

issues.t: Idle fluctuates with throttle sensor codes
issues.sym: The idle speed goes up and down, and the check engine light comes on with accelerator position sensor codes (P1271 to P1285).
issues.why: These years use an electronic throttle. Isuzu issued bulletins for idle fluctuation and accelerator position sensor codes, including a sensor adjustment procedure.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the shop to check the accelerator pedal sensor and its wiring against the Isuzu bulletin before replacing parts.

issues.t: Check engine light with ignition module code P1340
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P1340. The engine may run roughly or not at all.
issues.why: The 3.5L V6 uses an ion-sensing ignition module to identify cylinders. Isuzu released service information for code P1340, a fault in that module or its circuit.
issues.next: Have a shop that can follow the Isuzu bulletin diagnose the ion sensing module and wiring.

issues.t: Transmission codes P1640 or P1650 from the engine computer
issues.sym: The check engine or transmission light comes on with codes P1640 or P1650, sometimes with odd shifting.
issues.why: Isuzu issued a bulletin linking these codes to output driver circuits in the engine computer (PCM) that control transmission and other functions.
issues.next: Ask the shop to check the wiring and connectors from the PCM per the Isuzu bulletin before replacing the transmission or computer.

issues.t: Fuel line can separate in a frontal crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign in normal driving. The risk shows up only in a serious frontal crash.
issues.why: In some high-speed frontal crashes, an inner fuel line and hose could separate and leak fuel, which could start a fire. About 13,000 trucks were recalled (00V253000).
issues.next: Ask an Isuzu-authorized shop or call Isuzu with your VIN to confirm the fuel system shields were installed. If you smell fuel at any time, don't drive it.

issues.t: Fuel hose can leak in a crash on Torque-on-Demand models (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign in normal driving. The risk is a fuel leak after a hard frontal crash.
issues.why: On 4WD automatic Troopers with Torque-on-Demand, parts in the engine bay can shift in a high-speed frontal crash and damage a fuel hose. Isuzu recalled about 18,000 trucks (00V376000) to fit a reinforced hose.
issues.next: Confirm with your VIN that the reinforced fuel hose was installed. Any fuel smell or wet spot under the engine needs inspection before driving.

issues.t: Transfer case flange nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the truck, or sudden loss of drive if a driveshaft comes loose.
issues.why: On some early 1998 Troopers the nuts holding the driveshaft flanges on the transfer case were not staked and could back off. If one loosens fully, a driveshaft can separate. About 3,000 trucks were recalled (98V180000).
issues.next: Have the flange nuts checked if you can't confirm the recall was done. Stop driving if you feel a new vibration or clunk from underneath.

issues.t: Left front brake line rubs on the suspension (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid on the inside of the left front wheel, a soft or sinking pedal, or longer stops.
issues.why: The left front brake line was routed too close to the upper control arm and could be worn through, leaking fluid. About 6,700 trucks were recalled (97V092001).
issues.next: If the pedal is soft or you see fluid, don't drive it. Have the line clearance checked and confirm the recall with your VIN.

issues.t: Rear center seat belt buckle won't latch (recall)
issues.sym: The middle rear seat belt tongue will not click into its buckle.
issues.why: Some trucks were built with a rear center buckle meant for another market, so the belt cannot latch. About 2,300 trucks were recalled (96V248001).
issues.next: Don't seat anyone in the middle rear seat until the buckle is checked and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing nut can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding, wobble or play in a front wheel, or a front wheel locking up.
issues.why: A small number of 1997 Troopers were built with front hubs missing a lock washer or screws, so the bearing nut could loosen and the bearing seize (97V035001).
issues.next: If a front wheel grinds, wobbles or feels loose, stop driving and have the hub inspected.

issues.t: Valve ticking from the 3.2L V6
issues.sym: A light ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, often louder at startup.
issues.why: Varnish can make the hydraulic lash adjusters (lifters) stick. Isuzu issued a bulletin on valvetrain ticking for 1997 and earlier trucks, and a switch to synthetic oil has often cleared it.
issues.next: Make sure the oil level is full and the oil is fresh. If ticking continues after an oil change, have the valvetrain inspected.

issues.t: 4WD light on while in two-wheel drive
issues.sym: The 4WD indicator stays lit even though the truck is in two-wheel drive.
issues.why: Faulty vacuum solenoid valves for the front axle can leave the 4WD light on.
issues.next: Have the 4WD vacuum solenoids and hoses checked. It is usually not urgent, but confirm the front axle is disengaging properly.

issues.t: Frame and suspension mounts rust through
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, the truck pulling to one side, or visible flaking and holes in the frame or around the control arm and rear axle mounts.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, owners report frames and suspension mounting points rusting badly enough to crack or break.
issues.next: Have the frame and suspension mounts inspected on a lift, especially before buying. Severe rot can make the truck unsafe to drive.

issues.t: Manual transmission clutch fails
issues.sym: The clutch slips, the pedal feels wrong, a whine from the throwout bearing, or the truck won't go into gear.
issues.why: Owners of manual-transmission 1997 Troopers report clutch and throwout bearing failures that left them stranded, sometimes more than once.
issues.next: If the clutch slips or grinds, have it inspected before it leaves you stuck. Replace the clutch, bearing and hydraulic parts together.

issues.t: Windshield molding taps in the wind
issues.sym: A tapping or rattling sound from around the windshield at speed.
issues.why: Isuzu issued a bulletin for 1996-97 Troopers whose windshield molding makes a tapping noise.
issues.next: Ask a glass or body shop to secure or replace the molding.
